note: Hand-curated, sourced entries. Primary not yet held (Sept 8), frontrunners curated, not marked nominees.

NH-senate.statusNote: Open seat (Sen. Shaheen retiring). The primary is September 8. Chris Pappas (D) and John E. Sununu (R) lead their fields in UNH polling, but nominees aren't final.

candidates.name: Chris Pappas
candidates.background: U.S. Representative for NH-01 since 2019; family runs Manchester's Puritan Backroom restaurant. Leading the September 2026 Democratic primary field.

cost.label: Backs minimum-wage increases indexed to inflation; paid family leave (Ballotpedia; 2018 platform)

health.label: Supports public option / Medicare opt-in, drug-price negotiation (Ballotpedia)

immigration.label: Backs Dreamer citizenship pathway and comprehensive reform (Ballotpedia)

climate.label: Calls climate change 'an existential threat'; opposes offshore drilling off NH (Ballotpedia)

education.label: Tuition-free public college, universal pre-K; opposes diverting funds to private schools (Ballotpedia)

repro.label: 100% pro-choice record; led reversal of Planned Parenthood defunding (Ballotpedia)

housing.label: Mixed: authored a permitting pilot funding pre-approved 'pattern books' for missing-middle and infill building AND expanded FHA manufactured-home and accessory-dwelling financing for affordable housing (House office)

taxes.label: Against lowering the corporate rate, 'largest corporations...should pay a minimum tax'; raise the Social Security income cap; opposed the 2017 Trump tax plan (Citizens Count)

safety.label: Backed the George Floyd Justice in Policing Act, 'curtailing excessive use of force, and increasing accountability', and ending qualified immunity (Citizens Count)

democracy.label: Voted for the John R. Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act, H.R. 4, passed 219-212 (House roll call 260, 2021); also backs mail-in voting (House clerk)

candidates.name: John E. Sununu
candidates.background: U.S. Senator 2003–2009 and Representative 1997–2003, seeking his old seat; son of Gov. John H. Sununu and brother of Gov. Chris Sununu. Endorsed by President Trump. 2026 campaign theme: 'lower the temperature' in Washington.

immigration.label: Voted against the 2007 McCain-Kennedy reform; opposed legalization pathways (Wikipedia)

taxes.label: ATR 'Friend of the Taxpayer'; 100% Citizens Against Government Waste rating (Wikipedia)

climate.label: Mixed record: co-sponsored 2007 Clean Air Planning Act (cap-and-trade) but opposed 2003 Climate Stewardship Act (Wikipedia)

repro.label: Opposed abortion rights; among the most conservative House records on abortion (Wikipedia, citing Boston Globe)

cost.label: Opposed minimum-wage increases (Boston Globe, 2000); 100% Club for Growth rating, market and spending-restraint approach (Wikipedia)

health.label: Voted for both 2007 CHIP expansion bills that President Bush vetoed, H.R. 976 and H.R. 3963 (Senate roll call 403, 2007)

housing.label: Voted yea on HR 3221, the 2008 foreclosure-prevention law creating FHA rescue loans and a national affordable housing trust fund (Senate roll call 186)

education.label: Voted for both failed 2001 Armey amendments to fund private school vouchers, including a 50 million dollar voucher pilot (House Clerk roll calls 135 and 136)

safety.label: Voted yea on the 1997 Juvenile Crime Control Act, pushing more juveniles into adult prosecution with grants tied to tougher juvenile justice (House Clerk roll call 118)

democracy.label: Voted yea on the Help America Vote Act, funding voting modernization and provisional ballots while adding first-time voter ID checks (House Clerk roll call 489)
